item.title: Portrait Cut for Two Speakers

turns.text: Turn this into a 9:16 vertical clip. Show the man when he asks his question, then the woman when she answers, with each centred while talking. Keep all 10 seconds and the original audio. No captions.

item.tests: Tests speaker-aware portrait reframing of a two-person conversation without losing either speaking turn.

answer_sheet.Source and speakers: Use talk-two.mp4. The man asks the question and the woman answers.
answer_sheet.Layout and transitions: Centre the current speaker in a full-frame portrait crop; a clean cut at the speaker change is fine.
answer_sheet.Size and duration: 9:16 vertical, all 10 seconds; free-tier resolution is fine.
answer_sheet.Audio and text: Preserve the original conversation and sound, with no captions or added text.

must_haves: The output is a 9:16 portrait edit of the attached office conversation.
The man is centred and his face is fully visible during his question.
The woman is centred and her face is fully visible during her answer.
Both speaking turns remain in their original order, with the full 10 seconds and original audio in sync.
The image is not stretched and contains no added captions.

turns.text: Make this clip 9:16 vertical, keeping all 10 seconds and the original audio, with no captions. Show the man asking his question then the woman answering, quick pls.

dialog.agent:
I can’t reliably make this exact edit with the connected tools: they don’t offer precise 9:16 reframing while preserving the original audio unchanged.

The edit needs a **10-second, 9:16 sequence**: frame the man during his question, then cut the framing to the woman for her answer, keeping the original audio and adding no captions. No generation credits were spent.

turns.agent: I tried, but Magic Hour refused the edit because your account has insufficient credits. No video was generated and no credits were spent.

approvals.name: edit_video

style.prompt: Reframe this entire 10-second source clip into a 9:16 vertical portrait video. Preserve the original footage, people, dialogue, timing, and original audio unchanged. Keep all 10 seconds, with no trimming, speed changes, added speech, music, or sound effects. Begin with the framing focused on the man as he asks his question, then quickly switch the framing to the woman as she answers, following the actual speaker timing in the source. Use natural speaker-focused crops, preserving faces. No captions, subtitles, text overlays, or added graphics. Only change the framing to vertical; do not restyle or recreate the scene.
